name: Voltage Monitoring
overview: As we mentioned before, over and under voltage protection aren’t the only benefits that a phase monitoring relay renders. Such devices can also help you deal with Phase unbalance or phase asymmetry issues. This situation occurs when one or multiple line to line voltages do not match with each other. This results in unbalanced voltage, which leads to unbalanced current inside the motor winding. If this happens, the temperature of the windings will also increase.

Phase asymmetry can be caused due to an unbalanced transformer bank, an unstable utility supply, or because of unevenly distributed loads on the same power system. A under voltage monitoring relay can protect the motor from damage because of phase asymmetry by turning off the equipment as soon as such an issue is detected.

Another issue that a voltage detection relay can be effective against is phase loss, which occurs when one out of the three phases is lost. Phase loss can happen because of a broken wire, thermal overload, mechanical failure, or worn contact. If phase loss transpires, motors, compressors, and pumps with 3 phases will consume excess current.

This could result in the device becoming overheated and therefore unsafe. A good-quality voltage monitor relay will protect the system from damage in such a scenario by immediately switching the equipment off as soon as a phase loss is detected.

Sometimes voltages are attained at their maximum positive value. When this happens, it is called phase sequence. When it comes to a three-phase system, each of the three voltages should fall within the same magnitude while ensuring the frequency is displaced electrically by an angle of 120 degrees.
benefits: Phase sequence, phase loss, phase asymmetry protection
Protection against under and over frequency issues

name: Earth Leakage Monitoring
overview: Earth Leakage Relays (ELRs) constitute indispensable safeguarding apparatus within electrical infrastructures, meticulously engineered to discern and mitigate deleterious earth fault currents. These sophisticated protective devices continuously scrutinize current disparities between live conductors and earth pathways, instantaneously triggering corrective measures upon detecting anomalous leakage exceeding predetermined thresholds.

Modern earth leakage indicator feature comprehensive parameter configurability—spanning leakage sensitivity from 30mA to 30A, adjustable trip delays up to 10 seconds, and versatile auxiliary supply compatibility across 110-415V AC/DC ranges. Incorporating nano-crystalline core-balanced current transformers for enhanced precision, these relays provide instantaneous tripping at quintuple set values while offering diagnostic LED indicators, manual/remote reset capabilities, and RS485 communication protocols.

Their deployment spans diverse applications including low-tension control panels, mining operations, variable-speed drives, HVAC systems, and fire protection circuits—ensuring comprehensive electrical safety across industrial and commercial installations through continuous monitoring and rapid fault isolation.

An Earth Leakage Relay, or ELR, is an essential component in electrical systems due to its vital role in providing earth leakage protection. Its importance lies in the ability to detect and respond to potentially hazardous leakage currents that can lead to electric shocks or electrical faults.

The primary reason to use an earth leakage protection relay is to enhance electrical safety. It acts as a protective measure by continuously monitoring the current flowing between the live conductors and the earth. If an abnormal current or leakage exceeding the set threshold is detected, the earth fault monitoring relay initiates a protective action to prevent accidents or equipment damage.

name: Brown Out Timers
overview: Motor Protection Timer Relay

A Brownout Timer is a protective timing device designed to safeguard electrical and electronic equipment from the harmful effects of low-voltage (brownout) conditions. When the voltage drops below a safe threshold, the brown out timer disconnects the load and reconnects it only after the supply stabilizes for a preset time delay. This ensures that motors, compressors, control systems, and sensitive devices are shielded from voltage dips, frequent restarts, and premature failures.
Prevents motors, compressors, and electronics from damage caused by low-voltage conditions and sudden restarts.
Configurable delay ensures that the load reconnects only after the voltage stabilizes, preventing nuisance tripping.
By avoiding frequent restarts,brownout timers help reduce mechanical and thermal stress on equipment, improving service life.
